transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex, Samir, Lina (Redwood); Dana, Mark, Priya, Ethan (Nimbus)

Summary (auto): Quick review of latest INT8 and FP8 quant runs. INT8 looks promising on perf but small quality regressions in long-form generation; FP8 shows bigger perf wins but needs more stability testing. Action items for both sides.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, we are on for the weekly quantization sync. quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana Ortiz: hey Dana here, ML eng on the nimbus side.
[00:12] Mark Liu: Mark from infra, hi.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Priya here.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir (Redwood SE) - i'll go over the perf slides and results.
[00:22] Ethan Rowe: Ethan, data science.
[00:25] Alex Chen: great. Samir, you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:28] Samir Patel: yeah, sure. so high-level, we ran three builds: our FP16 baseline, INT8 quant where we applied per-channel symmetric quant on weights and KV cache kept in fp16, and an FP8-style prototype that uses dynamic exponent scaling.
[00:42] Samir Patel: INT8 gave about 1.6x throughput on your inference workload (batch sizes 1-8, sequence avg ~128). memory footprint dropped ~28% on the worker. p50 latency improved ~25% and p95 went down from ~220ms to ~150ms in our short tests.
[01:05] Dana Ortiz: 1.6x is good. what about FP8? we saw notes in the sheet that FP8 was faster.
[01:10] Samir Patel: FP8 was a bit more aggressive - we observed roughly 2.1x throughput vs FP16 and memory down ~40%. p95 improved to ~120ms in the same microbenchmarks but important caveat: FP8 runs had more variability and some instability after long runs, we hit a few soft OOMs and precision edge cases on long-context samples.
[01:33] Priya Shah: by instability do you mean model crashes? or degraded outputs?
[01:36] Samir Patel: no hard crashes, mostly degraded numerics leading to occasional token implausible outputs in narrow edge cases and one soft OOM on a 32k context test. the model continued but had to fall back several layers for a few steps, which impacted quality.
[01:49] Mark Liu: and the OOMs - are those predictable or random? we need to know for our dedicated plan because we can't have unexplained restarts.
[01:55] Samir Patel: more on the predictable side - triggered by very long sequences and when batch concurrency spikes. we think it's tied to how we manage KV cache in the FP8 path; some internal buffers weren't quantized-friendly yet.
[02:07] Dana Ortiz: okay. on quality, we ran the 500-prompt eval set you recommended. baseline FP16 scores for our metric (we use pairwise preference and a BLEU-ish token accuracy) were at 0.82. INT8 dropped to ~0.80 on aggregate, so about a 2-3% regression. FP8 dropped to ~0.78 on the same set.
[02:30] Ethan Rowe: those sound small but do they correlate with user-visible regressions? we were most worried about hallucinations in long-form summarization.
[02:37] Samir Patel: good question. for hallucinations specifically, manual spot checks showed only a slight uptick in hallucination rate with INT8 - maybe from 1.8% to 2.4% on that subset. FP8 had a larger uptick, about to 3.5%. again these are spot checks and the effect is concentrated in tricky prompts with many numerical facts and nested context.
[02:58] Priya Shah: that is a helpful framing. our bar is pretty high for summaries, we can't accept a +1% hallucination increase across the board.
[03:05] Alex Chen: understood. one path is to use INT8 for most requests and route more critical long-form or high-risk prompts to FP16 or a higher-precision variant. we can also do hybrid: keep KV cache at fp16 for long contexts and quantize others.
[03:19] Dana Ortiz: hybrid sounds reasonable. do you have routing primitives for that today?
[03:23] Samir Patel: yes, smart routing is built in - you can add rules by route or by token length, we can tag requests that match the high-risk criteria and route to FP16. we also have an automatic fallback if the quantized variant crosses a quality threshold based on quick evals.
[03:37] Mark Liu: from infra perspective, what's the CPU & memory overhead on the server side for maintaining mixed-precision caches? we worry about added complexity.
[03:45] Samir Patel: minimal CPU overhead; memory slightly higher than pure INT8 since we keep some buffers in fp16, so you get a middle ground: about ~18-22% memory reduction instead of 28-40%. the trade-off is better numeric stability.
[03:58] Priya Shah: can you remind us of the perf numbers if we do hybrid (INT8 for short, fp16 for >2k tokens)?
[04:04] Samir Patel: rough ballpark: overall throughput ~1.45x vs FP16 across your mix; p95 ~160ms. depends a lot on your real distribution; if long-form traffic is small share, numbers approach INT8.
[04:16] Ethan Rowe: on tuning, what knobs did you change? and which produced the most benefit?
[04:20] Samir Patel: main levers were per-channel quant granularity, smoothing/clip thresholds during calibration, and KV cache precision. Per-channel quantization reduced quant noise and gave better quality than per-tensor for your model. Clip threshold tuning during calibration saved about 0.6% quality while keeping most perf.
[04:36] Dana Ortiz: what about evaluation metrics - are you using ROUGE/bleu or a preference model?
[04:40] Samir Patel: we used your pairwise preference where available plus token-level accuracy (BLEU-like) and a small hallucination classifier for spot checks. we can run additional automated metrics if you want.
[04:50] Priya Shah: will the preference model be sensitive to small-scale numeric differences? sometimes it flags shorter outputs as worse even if they're concise.
[04:57] Samir Patel: yes that can happen; that's why we pair it with manual sampling and targeted checks. we also recommend a customer-side rubric for critical flows.
[05:07] Alex Chen: quick note on security / deployment: Priya asked last time about KMS and SSO. updates?
[05:12] Lina Gomez: yep, on Private we support external KMS/HSM integrations and SAML SSO; we can share our security pack and the doc with config steps. for Dedicated we can enable key wrapping with your KMS.
[05:23] Mark Liu: good. also we need audit logs and request-level tracing for compliance - is that part of the pilot?
[05:29] Lina Gomez: yes we can turn on request traces and the console provides token-level breakdowns. we'll include a sample trace export.
[05:34] Dana Ortiz: back to perf - can you share the raw perf spreadsheet? the one you uploaded had a few columns unnamed.
[05:38] Samir Patel: absolutely, i'll tidy the sheet and rename columns; Samir to share link after the call.
[05:45] Alex Chen: any other blockers from the customer's side for running the INT8 stability job?
[05:49] Dana Ortiz: we need the docker image and the exact run script plus env vars; otherwise we can kick off the 24h test. also we want to instrument memory/p95 and anomaly hooks.
[05:58] Samir Patel: we'll share a runbook and a reproducible docker image tag.
[06:03] Ethan Rowe: question - in your tests did you see any prompt amplification of hallucinations with repeated prefixes? like when we feed multi-turn context repeatedly?
[06:10] Samir Patel: yes, some amplification in FP8 tests on multi-turn with repeating system prompts; INT8 much less so but still visible in very long sessions. we recommend prefix trimming or periodic KV checkpointing for long sessions as mitigation.
[06:24] Priya Shah: timeline-wise, if we do the 24h INT8 run this week and share eval results next Monday, when can we get a Dedicated pricing delta?
[06:32] Alex Chen: I can get pricing delta for INT8 vs FP16 by Thursday, we'll include options for reserved capacity and burst.
[06:38] Samir Patel: also recommending a canary: run INT8 on 5% of requests for 24h in prod-like env to surface any oddities before wider rollout.
[06:47] Dana Ortiz: sounds good. we'll queue the 24h job once we get the image.
[06:51] Alex Chen: ok let's recap action items.
[06:54] Samir Patel: i'll share cleaned perf sheet, docker image tag, and runbook. i'll also start the 24h stability on our infra if we need but prefer customer to run in their environment - we'll help.
[07:06] Dana Ortiz: i'll run the eval set and send results.
[07:09] Alex Chen: i'll get pricing delta and schedule the infra deep dive next week.
[07:14] Priya Shah: thanks everyone.
[07:16] Alex Chen: thanks, end call.
